title: Lighthouse SLO Partnership Pilot Canvas
body:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight project canvas to run a Lighthouse SLO Partnership pilot across Product, Infra, Serving Runtime, and SRE. The goal is to create a repeatable pattern (playbook + automation) for onboarding a service to the Reliability Program, validate observability/data contracts, and prove that error-budget-driven runways + rollout gates reduce user-impact incidents for a bounded set of services.

Context and motivation:
- We need a reproducible, cross-functional cadence to operationalize SLOs that can be scaled across teams without heavy bespoke work per service.
- Previous SLO efforts stalled on gaps: missing data contracts, manual incident handoffs, and unclear rollout acceptance criteria.
- This pilot will focus on three "lighthouse" services (one product-facing API, one internal indexer, one realtime ingestion pipeline) to validate the pattern.

Goals (outcome-focused):
1) Establish production-grade SLOs for latency and availability for the three lighthouse services, with measurement accuracy >99% and sampling artifacts tracked.
2) Deliver an SLO onboarding checklist + automated audit (observability smoke tests) that catches common gaps (missing metrics, inconsistent tags, partial spans).
3) Integrate error-budget signals into the release runway: automatic rollback thresholds for canaries and a lightweight ops escalation ladder.
4) Capture a repeatable playbook and handoff artifacts so two additional teams can onboard within two sprints.

Success metrics (how we will know this worked):
- Each lighthouse service has SLOs and a verified measurement pipeline (Concordance score >= 0.95).
- Time to detect and route around a user-impacting degradation reduced by 35% vs baseline.
- Two additional teams complete onboarding using the playbook within 8 weeks of pilot close.
- No major P1 incidents attributable to SLO rollout automation within 30 days of cutover.

Scope (in-scope / out-of-scope):
- In-scope: Definition and measurement of SLOs (latency p95/p99 and availability), error budget policy for canary gating, observability data-contract checklist, playbook docs, automation scripts for canary rollback, and runbook for escalation.
- Out-of-scope: Full multi-region disaster recovery design, long-term billing optimization, and heavy-weight quota systems. Those will be follow-ups.

Key stakeholders and roles:
- SRE lead (owner): Priya Nair — overall pilot coordination and acceptance.
- Product engineer reps: Jasmine Liu (API product), Marco Santoro (indexer), Ethan Morales (ingestion).
- Infra/Serving Runtime: Ava Kim — ensure metrics + KV cache visibility.
- Observability eng: TBD — implement audit checks and dashboards.
- Customer Success & On-call rotation: consult for impact assessment and comms.

Workstreams (parallel):
1) Measurement & Data Contracts (Observability eng + Service owners)
   - Deliverables: metric schema, tagging convention, sampling plan, end-to-end latency tracing, and test harness for metric completeness.
   - Acceptance: audit pass (>=95%) for ingestion of required metrics into central telemetry.

2) SLO Definition & Policy (SRE + Product + Service owners)
   - Deliverables: SLO doc (owner, target, window, burn rate policy), error budget allocation, and canary gating thresholds.
   - Acceptance: signed SLO by product owner and SRE, canary failing a burn-rate test triggers rollback in the staging pipeline.

3) Automation & Runway (Platform eng + Release eng)
   - Deliverables: lightweight automation that reads burn-rate from telemetry and toggles canary weight or triggers rollback; playbook steps encoded as checklist items in CI.
   - Acceptance: simulated burn-rate test in staging causes expected automation action in controlled experiment.

4) Playbook & Onboarding (SRE + DevEx)
   - Deliverables: one-page onboarding checklist, runbooks, sample Jira templates, and a 60-minute onboarding session for the two follow-up teams.
   - Acceptance: two follow-up teams onboard within defined timeframe with minimal support.

5) Communication & Incident Integration (CS + On-call leads)
   - Deliverables: customer-facing impact taxonomy, internal alerting thresholds mapped to SLO degradation tiers, and an escalation ladder.

Pilot timeline (8 weeks, high-level):
- Week 0 (planning): Identify lighthouse services, confirm owners, baseline telemetry audit.
- Week 1-2 (measurement): Implement missing metrics, finalize data contracts, run initial audits.
- Week 3 (SLO definition): Draft SLOs and error budget policies; product sign-off.
- Week 4-5 (automation): Build simple automation for canary gating + rollback; run staging experiments.
- Week 6 (cutover rehearsal): Dry run on a non-critical canary; validate runbooks and communications.
- Week 7 (pilot cutover): Rollout SLO gating to one lighthouse service in production with monitoring and war-room standby.
- Week 8 (retro & handoff): Capture lessons, publish playbook, and initiate onboarding for next teams.

Key milestones & decision points:
- Milestone A (end of Week 2): Observability audit pass. Decision: proceed to SLO drafting or pause for remediation.
- Milestone B (end of Week 3): Product + SRE sign-off on SLOs. Decision: accept targets or recalibrate.
- Milestone C (end of Week 5): Automation smoke tests passed. Decision: proceed to production rehearsal.

Acceptance criteria for cutover:
- All required metrics ingested and validated in production telemetry for at least 72 hours.
- Automated canary gating exercised in staging with simulated burn.
- Communication plan approved (CS notified, on-call roster assigned).
- Incident playbook nodes (who does what) documented and accessible.

Observability-specific notes (novel patterns we will validate):
- Observability Data Contract: require a standard tag set (team, service, environment, deployment_id, trace_id) for all metrics and spans.
- Concordance checks: small service-side harness emits test traces to validate sampling fidelity end-to-end.
- SLO evaluation harness: a nightly regression that replays synthetic load and asserts SLO measurement stability.

Error budget mechanics and product integration:
- Error budgets will be treated as a release runway signal. When burn rate exceeds threshold, automation reduces canary weight; if sustained, the system triggers rollback.
- Product teams will see a feature flag 'slo-guard' that can be toggled during remediation windows. We will prototype the feature flag mapping for one product to validate the workflow.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Metrics gap in third-party components. Mitigation: create temporary synthetic checks and escalate to vendor integrations team; mark as known limitation in playbook.
- Risk: Excessive noise from immature alerts. Mitigation: tune alert thresholds in staging and use aggregated SLO signals rather than raw alerts for gating.
- Risk: Rollback automation false-positive. Mitigation: require two independent burn-rate windows or manual ack for first production cutover.

Open questions (to resolve in kickoff):
- Who owns concordance scoring policy and threshold?
- What is the exact mapping from SLO tier -> canary weight reduction steps?
- Which telemetry retention window is sufficient for accurate SLO windows (30d vs 90d)?

Immediate next steps (action items):
- [Priya] Book kickoff workshop with service owners and Observability eng (by 2026-02-16).
- [Ava] Draft metric tag contract and push to shared repo (by 2026-02-18).
- [Jasmine/Marco/Ethan] Baseline telemetry audit for each lighthouse service (by 2026-02-19).
- [Observability eng] Prototype concordance harness and share runbook (by 2026-02-26).

Notes & artifacts to capture in folder:
- SLO drafts (one per service)
- Observability audit checklist + raw audit outputs
- Automation scripts + CI docs
- Post-mortem template and onboarding slides

Tone: keep this lightweight, actionable, and timeboxed. We are aiming for a pilot that produces a minimal, repeatable artifact set rather than a heavy program launch. Use the playbook created here as the canonical starter for SLO onboarding across the Reliability Program.
